about.title: Palm Springs Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Springs sees a steady flow of traffic between Highway 111, Ramon Road, and Indian Canyon Drive, corridors that carry visitors, seasonal residents, and commuters alike. Riverside County recorded 268 injury collisions and 390 injured people in the most recent final year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday afternoons as weekend traffic builds. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the period right after matters: photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage can fade or disappear quickly in desert heat and busy repair schedules. LawProactive connects you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation and explain your options under California law. We're not a law firm and don't handle your case ourselves, but we can help you find someone who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. You focus on healing; let someone else sort out the insurance calls.

whyChoose.title: Why Palm Springs Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Are Real
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government entity (like a city vehicle or a road defect) is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early protects your ability to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your percentage isn't overstated by the other insurer.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. That matters after a serious crash, and an attorney can help make sure those losses aren't ignored in negotiations.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to minimize what they eventually pay. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Gene Autry Trail or another busy Palm Springs road?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors like Gene Autry Trail, Ramon Road, and Indian Canyon Drive see a large share of the city's reported collisions, especially on Friday afternoons. Location alone doesn't determine fault or value, but documenting exactly where and how the crash happened is important. An attorney can help gather traffic camera footage, witness statements, and police reports tied to that specific stretch of road.
